title: Forces and momentum

Terms and clues: A.2#c20 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; A.2#c31 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; A.2.11#xt1 term and clue written for the game; A.2.15#xt1 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electric force, F_e
items.clue: The field force between charged bodies: like charges repel and unlike charges attract.

items.label: Centripetal acceleration
items.clue: The rate of change of velocity for a body on a circular path, of size v squared over r.

items.label: Elastic collision
items.clue: An impact in which the total kinetic energy of the bodies is the same before and after.

items.label: Centripetal force
items.clue: The resultant, directed radially inwards, that changes a body's direction but not its speed.

questions.stem: An astronaut has a mass of 70.0 kg on Earth, where g = 9.8 N kg⁻¹. She travels to the Moon, where g = 1.62 N kg⁻¹. Which statement about the astronaut on the Moon is correct?

options.text: Her weight is 686 N.
Her mass is reduced.
Her weight is 113 N.
Her weight is 0.0 N.

questions.explanation: Mass does not depend on location, so it stays 70.0 kg. Weight is F_g = mg = 70.0 kg × 1.62 N kg⁻¹ = 113 N.

questions.stem: A ball is released from rest and falls towards the ground. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about momentum during the fall is correct?

options.text: The ball's momentum increases, while the total momentum of the ball and the Earth stays constant.
The ball's momentum stays constant, because momentum is conserved in every situation.
The ball's momentum stays constant, because its gain in E_k equals its loss in E_p.
The ball's momentum increases, and the Earth's is unchanged, as the ball cannot pull it.

questions.stem: A crate on a rough horizontal floor is pushed horizontally with a constant force of 40.0 N for 5.00 s. Throughout this time the crate slides forwards and the dynamic frictional force on it is 15.0 N. What is the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the crate by the resultant force during the 5.00 s?

options.text: 200 N s
125 N s
275 N s
5.0 N s

questions.explanation: The resultant force is 40.0 N − 15.0 N = 25.0 N forwards. The impulse of the resultant force is J = FΔt = 25.0 N × 5.00 s = 125 N s.

questions.stem: Which statement about field forces is correct?

options.text: A magnetic field exerts a force on a charged particle even when it is at rest.
An electric field exerts a force on a charged particle even when it is at rest.
A gravitational force acts on a body only where there is air around it.
An astronaut in orbit has no weight, as gravity does not act there.

questions.explanation: An electric field exerts a force F_e on any charge in it, whether the charge is moving or stationary. This is one of the differences between the electric and the magnetic force.

questions.stem: Under which condition does the total momentum of a system of interacting bodies remain constant?

options.text: When every collision between the bodies is elastic
When the bodies exert no forces at all on one another
When no resultant external force acts on the system
When every body in the system moves at a constant speed

questions.explanation: Forces between the bodies are internal and cancel in third-law pairs, so only an external resultant force can change the total momentum. With no resultant external force, the total momentum is constant, whatever happens inside the system.

questions.stem: A cricket ball is struck by a bat. During the short time of contact the force between the bat and the ball rises from zero to a maximum and then falls back to zero. Which statement about the impulse delivered to the ball is correct?

options.text: It is the product of the maximum force exerted on the ball and the total time of contact.
It is the product of the average resultant force on the ball and the time of contact.
It is the largest value reached by the resultant force on the ball during the contact.
It is the average resultant force on the ball divided by the total time of contact.
